model_output.verdict: Google and Dell Technologies catch my eye, but I’d hesitate over your current operations work at Brightline. The earlier program results are strong; the Austin terminal role leaves me guessing about the size of your team and what you’ve changed.
write_up: You moved from supply chain programs at Dell Technologies to data center capacity planning at Google, then into terminal operations at Brightline. It’s common for a current role to be written as a list of duties, but here that leaves your most recent management work less convincing than the older jobs.

Your Google line about cutting the forecast-to-delivery cycle works especially well: it names the starting point, the improvement and the approval change you made. A recruiter can see both the result and the work behind it.

Let’s start with the Austin terminal. Add how much work moves through it and how many people you manage, then show the issues and metrics you handle. That will give the current role more of the substance already present in your Google and Dell work.

cards.line: - Responsible for daily operations of the Austin terminal
cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter can’t tell which terminal operations are yours or how much freight moves through them. That makes it difficult to compare this role with other operations jobs.
cards.example: Responsible for daily operations of the Austin terminal, including [operations] and handling [volume and period]
cards.question: Which operations are you responsible for, and what volume does the terminal handle?

cards.line: - Manage a team of coordinators and dispatchers
cards.cannot_tell: Managing coordinators and dispatchers is relevant, but the team’s headcount and work are missing. Those details matter when a recruiter is comparing management roles.
cards.example: Manage a team of [number] coordinators and dispatchers who [what the team handles]
cards.question: How many coordinators and dispatchers do you manage, and what does the team handle?

cards.line: - Work with carriers and customers to resolve issues
cards.cannot_tell: Carriers and customers could bring you many kinds of problems. The line doesn’t say which ones you handle or what you do to resolve them.
cards.example: Work with carriers and customers to resolve [type of issue] by [your action]
cards.question: What kind of issue do you handle with carriers and customers, and what do you do to resolve it?

cards.line: - Report weekly metrics to the regional director
cards.cannot_tell: The weekly reporting is clear, but the metrics and their use aren’t. Those details would show what you track at the terminal.
cards.example: Report weekly [metrics] to the regional director for [how the metrics are used]
cards.question: Which metrics do you report, and how are they used?

cards.line: - Cut the forecast-to-delivery cycle for new capacity from 14 months to 9 by consolidating three approval tracks into one
cards.cannot_tell: Keep this as a model. It pairs a before-and-after measure with the decision you made, so the improvement isn’t just a number on its own.

fit.why: Your current role manages terminal operations and a team of coordinators and dispatchers.
fit.note: Your earlier capacity planning and supply chain programs give you another strong part of the story. For terminal roles, bring the current job closer to that standard with details about the work and team.
